title: AI Excuse Court
oneLiner: A playful classroom dispute simulator where teachers rehearse parent/student AI-cheating conversations and turn drama into a fair paper trail.
targetUser: Teachers, department leads, and school trainers navigating AI-writing accusations, parent emails, detector uncertainty, and admin pressure for phone calls.
keyUx: Choose a scenario, cross-examine the student/parent/admin, collect evidence cards, test policy-safe wording, and export a neutral communication trail that avoids false certainty while still protecting the teacher.
requiredUiSections: evidence card table: assignment, drafts, detector note, rubric
externalSignals: Signal 7 — Reddit r/Teachers AI-checker panic and parent emails: https://www.reddit.com/r/Teachers/comments/1p85k9h/my_students_discovered_ai_checkers_and_are_now/
stitchPrompt: Design a playful web prototype called AI Excuse Court for teachers rehearsing AI-cheating disputes with students, parents, and admins. The user should pick a classroom scenario, inspect evidence cards such as assignment instructions, draft history, rubric notes, and AI-detector caveats, cross-examine a parent/student argument simulator, compose policy-safe wording, and export a neutral paper trail. Include a case docket scenario picker, evidence card table, parent/student argument simulator, policy-safe response composer, paper-trail export preview, and absurd verdict badge wall. Design direction: use a playful-experimental aesthetic with courtroom-game metaphors, expressive but readable cards, witty microcopy, dramatic stamps, and bright accent colors while keeping the final export calm, fair, and professional.
